Read a metabolic cart export

Source: R/read_cart.R
read_cart.Rd

Reads the breath-by-breath export of a metabolic cart, averages it into fixed intervals and returns the tables that [MFO()] expects, in the package's internal data contract (SPEC 16). This is the only layer that knows the proprietary formats.

Usage

read_cart(
  file,
  device = NULL,
  interval = 10,
  cuts = NULL,
  phase = c("MFO", "basal", "graded"),
  body_mass = NULL,
  vo2_unit = c("auto", "mL/min", "L/min", "mL/kg/min"),
  columns = NULL,
  skip = 0,
  units_row = FALSE,
  decimal = c(".", ","),
  sheets = NULL,
  time_origin = c("elapsed", "clock")
)

Arguments

file

path of the export.

device

`NULL` (detected by spiro), `"cortex"`, `"cosmed"`, `"vyntus"`, `"zan"`, or `"generic"` for a csv/xlsx file with mapped columns (does not need spiro).

interval

length of the averaging intervals in seconds (default 10), or `"none"` for records already averaged by the analyser; it becomes `step_time` for [MFO()].

cuts

optional named vector of cut times in seconds, with `basal_end` and/or `MFO_end`.

phase

without `cuts`, the phase of the whole recording: `"MFO"` (default), `"basal"` or `"graded"`.

body_mass

body mass in kg, needed only when `vo2_unit = "mL/kg/min"`.

vo2_unit

unit of VO₂ and VCO₂ in the export: `"auto"` (default), `"mL/min"`, `"L/min"` or `"mL/kg/min"`.

columns, skip, units_row, decimal, sheets, time_origin

for `device = "generic"` only: column mapping (named character vector), lines before the header (default 0), whether a units row follows the header (default `FALSE`), decimal mark (`"."` or `","`), xlsx sheets per phase, and whether `Time` is `"elapsed"` (default) or `"clock"` time. See *Generic files*.

Value

An object of class `MFO_cart`: a list with `db_basal`, `db_MFO`, `db_graded` (data frames with `Time`, `VO2`, `VCO2`, `RER` and, when the export has them, `HR`, `Load`, `VE`; `NULL` for a phase not in the file), `step_time` (= `interval`, or the step of `Time` with `interval = "none"`) and `info` (device, interval, averaging, VO₂ unit, cuts, `time_origin` and `time_offset` for generic files, number of breaths or records, of intervals and of empty intervals, and the RER mismatch count, `NA` when the export has no RER).

Details

The file is parsed with `spiro::spiro_raw()` (package spiro, rOpenSci, JOSS 2023; in Suggests), which reads Cortex (MetaSoft Studio), Cosmed (Omnia, Quark CPET, K5), Vyaire Vyntus CPX (SentrySuite) and ZAN exports. MFO has validated none of these devices with a real export of its own yet (one anonymised file per device is planned in `inst/extdata`); ZAN is tested only with the example files of spiro.

**Averaging.** The breaths are averaged in consecutive intervals of `interval` s from time 0: each value is the mean of the breaths measured in that interval, not an interpolation. An interval without breaths is kept as a row of `NA`, so the records stay aligned in time (`MFO()` cuts steps by counting records). The default of 10 s divides the usual step durations (60-300 s) and the 30-s windows of VO₂max and ramps exactly, so they need no rounding.

**Units.** VO₂ and VCO₂ are returned in mL/min. With `vo2_unit = "auto"` a median VO₂ above 100 is read as mL/min; at or below 100 the unit must be given, because L/min and mL/kg/min cannot be told apart reliably. RER is always VCO₂/VO₂ of the interval means; when the export has its own RER, a warning counts the intervals where they differ by more than 0.02. Load is passed through unconverted: declare its unit in [MFO_protocol()].

**Phases.** `cuts` gives the times (s from the start) at which the resting measure ends (`basal_end`) and the MFO test ends (`MFO_end`). With both, the recording is split into basal, MFO and graded tables; with `MFO_end` only, into MFO and graded (a single-day test, see [MFO_protocol()]); with `basal_end` only, into basal and MFO. Without `cuts`, the whole recording is the phase named in `phase`. Detecting the phases from the analyser's markers will come with each device importer.

**Generic files** (`device = "generic"`). A csv or xlsx file whose columns are mapped with `columns`, as `col_name_*` in [MFO()] (SPEC 16):

  • `columns` maps the contract names `Time`, `VO2`, `VCO2` and, optionally, `RER`, `HR`, `Load` and `VE` to the names in the file, e.g. `c(Time = "t", VO2 = "VO2 STPD")`; names not given are looked up as they are. Names must match exactly; a missing column stops with the list of columns in the file.

  • `skip` lines (e.g. metadata) come before the header; with `units_row = TRUE` the line after the header holds the units. A recognised VO₂ unit there ("mL/min", "L/min", "mL/kg/min") is taken as a declaration of the file, with a message; an explicit `vo2_unit` wins.

  • `decimal` is the decimal mark (default "."); the csv field separator (tab, ";" or ",") is detected from the header line.

  • `Time` is in seconds, mm:ss, hh:mm:ss or Excel times (fractions of a day), detected automatically. With `time_origin = "elapsed"` (default) it is the time from the start of the recording; a first value above 1 h stops with an error suggesting `"clock"`. With `time_origin = "clock"` (time of day), the first value is subtracted, so Time counts from the first record, and the value subtracted is kept in `info$time_offset`.

  • Records already averaged by the analyser (e.g. every 20 s) are read with `interval = "none"`: they are kept as they are and `step_time` is the step of `Time`, which must be regular. A numeric `interval` is for breath-by-breath files.

  • `sheets` reads the phases from the sheets of an xlsx file, `c(basal = , MFO = , graded = )` (any of them), as an alternative to `cuts`; one unnamed sheet is the recording, the phase named in `phase` or split by `cuts`.

No personal data from the file are kept: the result holds only the measured variables and technical information.

Warnings and messages

Every warning and message of this function is a classed condition: `mfo_warning_<id>` and `mfo_warning` (or `mfo_message_<id>` and `mfo_message`), with the numbers of the text as fields (for example `mfo_warning_negative_fat` has `n`, the number of steps). The text is English; the classes let a program, such as [run_app()], handle a given warning or word it in another language: `withCallingHandlers(expr, mfo_warning_negative_fat = function(w) w$n)`.

See also

[MFO()], [MFO_protocol()]

Examples

# A generic csv: metadata line, header, units row, decimal comma, records
# already averaged every 20 s (the example MFO test, VO2 in L/min)
data(MFO_df, package = "MFO")
t <- seq_len(nrow(MFO_df)) * 20
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(c("Example export;MFO test",
             "t;VO2;VCO2;FC;Watts",
             "mm:ss;L/min;L/min;1/min;W",
             sprintf("%02d:%02d;%s;%s;%s;%s", t %/% 60, t %% 60,
                     sub(".", ",", MFO_df$VO2 / 1000, fixed = TRUE),
                     sub(".", ",", MFO_df$VCO2 / 1000, fixed = TRUE),
                     sub(".", ",", MFO_df$HR, fixed = TRUE), MFO_df$Load)), f)
cart <- read_cart(f, device = "generic", interval = "none", skip = 1,
                  units_row = TRUE, decimal = ",",
                  columns = c(Time = "t", HR = "FC", Load = "Watts"))
#> VO2 and VCO2 unit taken from the units row: L/min.
cart
#> <MFO_cart> generic, 20-s records as exported, VO2 in L/min
#>   MFO       72 intervals (0-1440 s)
#>   72 records; 0 empty interval(s)
head(cart$db_MFO)
#>   Time VO2 VCO2       RER   HR Load
#> 1   20 635  487 0.7669291 90.2   25
#> 2   40 627  479 0.7639553 94.9   25
#> 3   60 634  468 0.7381703 93.3   25
#> 4   80 646  486 0.7523220 95.6   25
#> 5  100 630  483 0.7666667 93.5   25
#> 6  120 679  517 0.7614138 99.4   25

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("spiro", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # A graded test exported by a ZAN cart (example file of spiro)
  cart <- read_cart(spiro::spiro_example("zan_gxt"), phase = "graded")
  cart
  VO2max_from_test(cart$db_graded, step_time = cart$step_time)
}
#> Warning: age not given: the heart-rate criterion of VO2max is not evaluated.
#> <MFO_VO2max> VO2peak = 4727.2 ml/min (highest 30-s mean)
#>   plateau  not met        value 1655.019, threshold 150
#>   RER      not met        value 0.991, threshold 1.1
#>   HR       not evaluated  value NA, threshold 0.9
# }
